title: Life in the UK — Exam 19 · Weakness Revision
notes: 22 learner-provided weak questions plus 2 supplementary existing-exam questions.
Original question wording preserved; authored answers for previously missing items.
Dolly cloned from an adult cell and born in 1996, announced 1997; John Logie Baird London–Glasgow broadcast 1932.
Earlier exam data and progress remain unchanged.

questions.question: When was the Bill of Rights passed?
questions.explanation_original: The Bill of Rights was passed in 1689 following the Glorious Revolution.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: In which year was Dolly the sheep born as the first mammal cloned from an adult cell?
questions.explanation_original: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996, and the achievement was announced on 22 February 1997. Other mammals had been cloned earlier from embryonic cells; Dolly was the first cloned from an adult cell.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Scotland was joined to England in 1707 but retained which of the following?

options.text: Its own legal system, education system and established Church
A separate army and foreign policy

questions.explanation_original: The 1707 Union united the kingdoms, but Scotland retained distinct legal and education systems and the Church of Scotland.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: What happened in Northern Ireland in 1972?

options.text: Direct rule from Westminster was imposed after the Northern Ireland Parliament was suspended.
The Good Friday Agreement was signed.
Northern Ireland became an independent republic.

questions.explanation_original: In 1972, the UK government suspended the Northern Ireland Parliament and imposed direct rule from Westminster. Bloody Sunday also occurred in 1972.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: What is the Turner Prize?
questions.explanation_original: The Turner Prize was established in 1984 and celebrates contemporary art. The Turner Prize is recognised as one of the most prestigious visual art awards in Europe.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: Sir Francis Drake completed his circumnavigation of the globe in which year?
questions.explanation_original: Sir Francis Drake returned to England in 1580 after circumnavigating the globe.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Hitler became Chancellor of Germany in which year?
questions.explanation_original: Hitler became Chancellor of Germany in January 1933.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Which method is used to allocate most ministerial positions in the Northern Ireland Executive proportionally among parties?
questions.explanation_original: The d’Hondt method allocates most Northern Ireland Executive ministerial posts in proportion to Assembly party strength. It is part of the power-sharing arrangements but not the name of the entire arrangement; First Minister and deputy First Minister and Justice Minister are selected differently.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: What is the Caledonian Canal?

options.text: A canal across the Scottish Highlands connecting the east and west coasts
A river forming the England-Scotland border
A tunnel beneath the English Channel
A canal connecting London and Birmingham

questions.explanation_original: The Caledonian Canal links Inverness and Fort William through the Scottish Highlands.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: The Boers, whom Britain fought in the Boer War, were settlers originally from which country?
questions.explanation_original: The Boers were descendants principally of Dutch settlers in southern Africa.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: On what date did the D-Day landings in Normandy take place?
questions.explanation_original: The Allied D-Day landings in Normandy began on 6 June 1944.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: The scientist Ernest Rutherford, who first split the atom, was born in which country?
questions.explanation_original: Ernest Rutherford was born in New Zealand and worked in atomic physics in Britain.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Which classic film, about British athletes, was directed by Hugh Hudson in 1981?
questions.explanation_original: Chariots of Fire (1981), directed by Hugh Hudson, follows British athletes preparing for the 1924 Olympic Games.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: Durham, Lincoln, Canterbury and Salisbury are famous examples of what?
questions.explanation_original: Durham, Lincoln, Canterbury and Salisbury are famous English cathedral cities.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Who became the first Tudor monarch after the Wars of the Roses?
questions.explanation_original: Henry Tudor defeated Richard III at Bosworth Field in 1485 and became Henry VII, first Tudor monarch.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: The Scottish Parliament was established in:
questions.explanation_original: The modern Scottish Parliament first met in 1999, following the 1997 referendum on devolution.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a jury in a UK court?

options.text: To decide the sentence after conviction.
To decide whether the accused person is guilty or not guilty.
To bring criminal charges against a suspect.
To write new laws for Parliament.

questions.explanation_original: In a criminal trial, the jury decides whether the accused is guilty or not guilty on the evidence presented. The judge handles the law and sentencing.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: What is the longest river in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation_original: The River Severn is generally recognised as the longest river in the UK; the Thames is often mistaken for it.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: Henry V's great victory at Agincourt in 1415 was fought against:
questions.explanation_original: King Henry V defeated the French army at the Battle of Agincourt in 1415, during the Hundred Years' War.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: John Logie Baird made the first television broadcast between London and Glasgow in which year?
questions.explanation_original: For the Life in the UK study guide, the London–Glasgow television broadcast is dated to 1932. Do not confuse this with Baird's earlier television demonstrations.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: Bonnie Prince Charlie's Jacobite rebellion ended at which battle?
questions.explanation_original: The Jacobite rising was defeated at Culloden in 1746.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: Which Anglo-Saxon poem tells of its hero's battles against monsters?

options.text: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight

questions.explanation_original: Beowulf is an Old English epic featuring fights with Grendel, his mother and a dragon.
review_notes: Learner supplied question stem; choices and explanation newly authored.

questions.question: When was the Magna Carta created?
questions.explanation_original: The Magna Carta was created in 1215.
review_notes: Reused from an existing LifeUK exam.

questions.question: In which of the following matters can the Scottish Parliament legislate?
questions.explanation_original: The Scottish Parliament can legislate on: civil and criminal law, health, education, planning and additional tax-raising powers.
